I am a research scientist at Boston University School of Public Health. My primary research interests focus on estimating the impacts of climate hazards, air pollution, and built environment on human health across the life course under a changing climate, especially for susceptible populations, such as the fetus, children, pregnant women, and the older adults. Prior to Boston University, I was a postdoctoral research associate at Brown University School of Public Health. I received a PhD in epidemiology and biostatistics from the University of Hong Kong (2017) and earned a MSc in Environmental Health from Peking University (2013).
